title: Synthetic transaction readiness tiering and region-aware probe weighting to preserve SLOs during multi-region failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Our current readiness/liveness probes are single-tier HTTP checks ( /health, /ready ) with uniform weighting across regions. During regional disturbances or partial degradations this leads to noisy autoscaler decisions, excessive cross-region failovers, and violations of customer SLO windows (p99 latency and availability). Problem: simple binary probes do not capture degradation modes (slow tails, partial feature failures) and autoscaler reacts poorly when only a subset of requests are impacted. Additionally, circuit breakers and region failover logic are not probe-aware, which causes aggressive failovers and cascading capacity churn. Goal: implement a probe architecture that uses synthetic transactions (lightweight end-to-end requests), readiness tiering (fast-local, synthetic-tier, slow-degradation tier), and region-aware probe weighting so autoscaler and circuit-breakers make graded decisions that prioritize SLO preservation and minimize unnecessary cross-region failovers. This ticket covers design + implementation of server-side probe tiers, control-plane weighting, and integration with autoscaler heuristics and circuit-breaker policies. Scope: - Server probe endpoints and internal synthetic transaction runner - Probe tier definitions and thresholds (fast-path, synthetic-e2e, degraded-state) - Region-aware probe weighting in control plane (assign per-region contribution to overall health) - Autoscaler input transformation (smoothed health signal, token-based backpressure) - Circuit-breaker changes to prefer local degraded mode over immediate cross-region failover - Observability: metrics, alerting rules, and dashboards - Canary rollout plan and rollback hooks Non-goals: changing client-side retry semantics, reshaping model serving kernels, or altering billing logic.
acceptance_criteria: Introduced synthetic transaction probe that executes a lightweight model path and returns latency + error codes within 30ms median in normal conditions.
Control plane exposes three-tier readiness state per instance: GREEN (fast-path ok), AMBER (synthetic slow or errors), RED (unhealthy).
Autoscaler uses weighted regional health (configurable) and reduces scale-down aggressiveness when region is AMBER to avoid premature cross-region failover.
Circuit-breaker policy updated so small AMBER windows trigger degraded-mode routing (reduced concurrency, cache-first paths) before full failover.
Rollout executed to 10% traffic in us-west-2 and us-east-1 with metric validation showing no >5% p99 degradation or increased cost >8% during canary.
Documentation and runbook updated: Confluence design doc, Grafana dashboards, and on-call playbook for degraded mode.
End-to-end tests and chaos test harness coverage for transient AMBER windows and regional outage scenarios.
PRs merged and release tagged runtime-1.22 with migration flags off by default for existing customers.

notes: Decision summary: we chose synthetic lightweight model calls (no KV cache warm-up) instead of ping-only endpoints to capture tail latency anomalies. To avoid extra cost, synthetic probes run at low QPS (configurable per-region) and are sampled heavier during deploys and outages. Trade-offs: slightly higher control-plane complexity and additional probe metrics vs much lower cross-region failovers and better SLO adherence. Implementation will be guarded behind a feature flag per deployment tier.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Synthetic probes can increase load on the serving layer -> Mitigation: low sampled QPS, backpressure tokens and circuit-breaker prioritization for probe traffic.
Risk: Misconfigured regional weights could mask real outages -> Mitigation: default conservative weighting, auto-escalation if error counts exceed absolute thresholds.
Risk: Added complexity in autoscaler may introduce bugs -> Mitigation: staged rollout, canary, and e2e chaos tests with rollback hooks.
Risk: Observability gaps -> Mitigation: required dashboards and alerting thresholds as part of acceptance criteria.
